title: What If Earth Suddenly Lost Its Atmosphere?

scenes.text: What if Earth lost its air overnight? The oceans would be the first to go.
With no air pressure, water's boiling point drops. Seas, lakes and rivers would boil away into space.
You'd have about fifteen seconds of useful consciousness before you blacked out.
Temperatures would swing like the Moon's: roughly 121 degrees Celsius in sunlight and minus 133 at night.
Air also traps heat. Models put the average falling from about 15 degrees Celsius to around minus 18.
Almost everything would die. Only tough survivors like tardigrades handled ten days in a vacuum.

description:
What if Earth lost its atmosphere?
Oceans boiling away, fifteen seconds to blackout, and Moon-like swings between 121 and minus 133 degrees Celsius.
What should we run through next?
